title: Stroke and TIA: the urgent work-up and secondary prevention

source.citation: Written for Blackout, 2026-09-13. Based on the 2021 AHA/ASA secondary stroke prevention guideline and the 2019 acute ischaemic stroke guideline. Not tied to an article; review before trusting.

questions.q: A patient describes an hour of arm weakness and slurred speech yesterday, now fully resolved. What is the urgency?
questions.a: Evaluation within 24 to 48 hours, with imaging, vascular imaging and an ECG
d: Routine clinic follow-up in a month
Admission only if it happens again
questions.why: The risk of a completed stroke is highest in the first days after a transient ischaemic attack. Rapid clinics that see patients within a day cut that risk substantially.

questions.q: Which imaging best confirms that a transient event was ischaemic and shows any infarct?
questions.why: CT is the acute test to exclude haemorrhage. MRI finds the small infarcts that CT misses and turns many TIAs into minor strokes on the record, which changes the risk estimate.

questions.q: After a minor stroke or high-risk TIA, dual antiplatelet therapy with aspirin and clopidogrel is given for how long?
questions.why: Started within 24 hours, then a single agent. Long-term dual therapy adds bleeding without reducing stroke. Ticagrelor with aspirin for 30 days is an alternative.

questions.q: A stroke is attributed to atrial fibrillation. What is the long-term prevention?
questions.a: Oral anticoagulation, usually a direct oral anticoagulant
questions.why: It usually starts within 4 to 14 days, sooner for small infarcts and later for large ones, to balance recurrence against haemorrhagic transformation.

questions.q: Symptomatic carotid stenosis of 70% to 99%. Within how long should endarterectomy be done for greatest benefit?
questions.why: The benefit falls steeply with delay. Stenosis of 50% to 69% benefits less, and under 50% is treated medically.

questions.q: After an atherosclerotic ischaemic stroke, what LDL cholesterol is targeted?
questions.why: A high-intensity statin first, with ezetimibe added if needed. The target came from a trial that showed fewer recurrent events at 70 than at 100.

questions.q: What blood pressure target is recommended after a stroke or TIA?
questions.why: Thiazides and ACE inhibitors or ARBs have the best evidence. Acute blood pressure in the first days is a separate matter and is usually left higher.

questions.q: Up to how many hours from symptom onset can intravenous thrombolysis be given for ischaemic stroke?
questions.why: Mechanical thrombectomy for a large vessel occlusion extends to 24 hours with imaging selection. The intern's job is the time of onset and a fast call to the stroke team.

questions.q: A 45-year-old has a cryptogenic stroke and a patent foramen ovale with a large shunt. Which intervention reduces recurrence?
questions.why: Closure plus antiplatelet beat antiplatelet alone in patients under 60 with no other cause found. Atrial fibrillation must be excluded first with prolonged monitoring.

questions.q: An ischaemic stroke with no atrial fibrillation found on the admission ECG or telemetry. What is done about the rhythm?
questions.a: Prolonged monitoring, since paroxysmal atrial fibrillation is often missed
questions.why: Thirty days of monitoring, or an implantable loop recorder in cryptogenic stroke, finds atrial fibrillation in a meaningful minority and changes the treatment from antiplatelet to anticoagulant.

questions.q: After a stroke, which is recommended for secondary prevention in a smoker with diabetes?
questions.a: Smoking cessation, glucose control, a statin, blood pressure control and an antithrombotic
questions.why: The combination roughly halves recurrence. Each element is a separate conversation, and the drugs are started before discharge.

questions.q: A patient on aspirin has a second ischaemic stroke. What is the long-term antiplatelet plan?
questions.a: A single agent, often switched to clopidogrel; not permanent dual therapy
questions.why: Permanent dual antiplatelet therapy raises bleeding without lowering stroke. A stroke on aspirin also prompts a search for atrial fibrillation or a carotid lesion that was missed.
